neighbours.label: inside a romanised transliteration of a non-Latin name, mostly Tibetan-style consonant clusters
fire: The abbot (bSod nams rgyal mtshan) built the temple.
The scholar (Blo bzang grags pa) wrote the commentary.
The translator (rNgog lo tsā ba) visited Kashmir.
The yogi (Mi la ras pa) sang in the caves.
The master (dPal ldan ye shes) taught the novices.
The minister (mGar sTong btsan) served the king.
The queen (bKra shis mtsho mo) ruled the valley.
Tulu (tuḷu) and Malayalam (malayāḷam) are spoken in the south.
quiet: The abbot (Thomas Becket) built the temple.
The scholar (Peter Lombard) wrote the commentary.
The translator (Jerome of Stridon) visited Rome.
The poet (William Blake) sang in the taverns.
The master (James Bell) taught the novices.
The minister (Robert Walpole) served the king.
The queen (Mary Stuart) ruled the kingdom.
French (français) and Spanish (español) are spoken in the south.

notes: The fires are mid-transliteration tokens. A familiar European name in the same parenthetical is the near miss. A short word in parentheses, '(mgon po)', stayed quiet in a probe, so this is not all Wylie.
